newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran to take delivery of third submarine this week.
newsitem.headline: Iran to take delivery of third submarine this week.

text.p: Iran is expected to take delivery of a third Russian-made submarine this week, boosting its naval power in a region that controls 70 percent of the world's oil, British officers said on Wednesday.
The submarine will arrive in Bandr Abbas in Iran after a few days, Lieutenant Keith Blount, spokesman on the British guided missile destroyer HMS Southampton, told reporters.
The diesel-powered submarine left for Iran from Russia in November and passed through Egypt's Suez Canal on January 2.

"...A submarine threat in the area is another dimension which is relatively new...Everybody who is interested in stability in the region must take account of it," Duncan Potts, commander of the Southampton, said.
"Obviously as a potential threat it cannot be ignored," added the captain whose vessel is on a visit to Kuwait.

Gulf Arab states and Western navies deployed in the region are expected to keep a close watch once Iran deploys the third submarine to see if the Islamic republic had overcome technical problems operating the vessels, defence experts said.

Non-Arab Iran is the only regional power to deploy submarines in the Gulf area. The first of the three submarines joined the service in November 1992 while the second joined in June 1993, triggering keen interest by neighbours in anti-submarine warfare technology and weapons.
